title: Event
description: L0 contract. An Event is the atomic, append-only unit of ground truth in the log (urd). It is written once and never mutated or deleted. It is bi-temporal: occurred_at is when the thing happened in the world, recorded_at is when orlog learned about it. Any PII in payload must already be pseudonymized before the event is appended (principle 11 in DESIGN-PRINCIPLES.md) — this schema does not and cannot enforce that, it is a caller obligation.

event_id.description: Unique identifier for this event. Assigned once at append time, never reassigned.

event_type.description: What kind of thing happened, e.g. 'user_message', 'tool_call', 'fact_stated', 'correction', 'verification_outcome'. Deliberately a free-form string, not an enum: orlog keeps one event stream for everything (principle 8), so the set of event types is open-ended.

occurred_at.description: When the event happened in the world.

recorded_at.description: When orlog appended this event to the log. Must not be earlier than occurred_at.

source.description: Where this event came from, e.g. 'user', 'agent', 'tool:pytest'.

subject_ids.description: Stable pseudonym IDs for entities this event is about, if any.

payload.description: The actual content of the event. Structure is event_type-specific and not constrained further at this layer.
